positions.as_written: Identify the abnormal area within the tendon, since fenestration targets that tissue specifically.
Identify the sheath or peritendinous space as a separate compartment.
Identify any calcification and its acoustic shadow, which is the lavage target.
Keep the needle in plane and confirm which compartment the tip is in.
Record which compartment was entered, because the procedures are different.
Calcific deposits reflect strongly and cast a shadow, which is both how they are found and why a needle approaching them must be angled rather than blocked.
